Tests, styles, translations, and fixtures cover the new settings and capture flows.| **Estimated code review effort:** 4 (Complex) | ~60 minutes **Change:** Feature · **Severity of issue fixed:** Medium ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant ScreenshotIPC participant WorkspaceSettings participant CaptureHandler participant ScreenshotEditor ScreenshotIPC->>WorkspaceSettings: Refresh active workspace settings ScreenshotIPC->>CaptureHandler: Start capture CaptureHandler->>WorkspaceSettings: Read workspace and copy preference CaptureHandler-->>ScreenshotEditor: Return capture with policy ScreenshotEditor->>ScreenshotEditor: Apply captured copy policy ```
Merge Risk: Low · previous review 54305
A capture during workspace ID adoption may use the wrong copy preference and fall back instead of saving. Fix that boundary before merging; also make the race test’s ordering explicit.
Security architecture risk: Moderate · up to 54305
Folder settings have strong validation and consent controls, and upload preferences remain local to the device. However, adopting a returning workspace’s identity can leave capture policy and workspace ownership out of sync, potentially applying the wrong automatic-copy preference. **Retained concerns** - **Medium · security · inferred:** A capture-start refresh can split workspace identity from settings and gate ownership. When availability adopts provisional ID P as folder ID R, refresh(P) still caches the folder read under P and skips its change notification because P is no longer active. Capture then snapshots R with stale effective settings, while the gate can still name P. Saving under R is rejected before requireCaptureWorkspace can repair adoption, and the editor fallback retains the captured policy. If R has a previously accepted manual-copy override while the stale effective value is automatic, the capture can carry the wrong automatic-copy intent. The new pre-capture refresh introduces this ordering ahead of the existing adoption repair point; normal workspace switching and exact-hash validation do not repair this path.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The identified identity-transition concern is bounded to the desktop application’s workspace policy, screenshot persistence, and automatic-copy intent. Vault admission rejects a mismatched workspace ID rather than redirecting the screenshot into another workspace. No remote service compromise or upload-consent bypass was established. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _inferred_ — A returning folder can cause provisional-to-folder identity adoption during the new settings refresh. Because the read remains associated with the provisional ID, the subsequently captured policy need not represent the adopted workspace’s accepted overrides. This is a privacy-policy consistency failure path; exploitation by an external actor and actual clipboard disclosure were not demonstrated. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — Folder bytes do not directly authorize effective settings: activation requires local hash consent, and pending resolution rereads the file and rejects a changed hash. Renderer settings operations can deliberately target a selected non-active workspace. Global renderer settings authority already existed at the base, so missing sender or active-workspace checks alone do not establish a newly introduced authorization vulnerability. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Unavailable or timed-out folder probes make folder overrides inactive. Pending and unreadable files block folder mutations, and failed folder writes attempt to restore the previous machine-local hash record. A missing capture policy falls back to the editor without automatic copying. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Make identity adoption, gate rebinding, and effective-settings refresh one completed transition before capturing privacy policy. If identity changes during a probe, refresh under the resolved ID and notify consumers before allowing a policy snapshot.

Full details: Title check
**Explanation** The title "feat(settings): per-workspace settings with inheritance (NIW2-601)" names the main change. The changeset adds per-workspace overrides for five settings, with All-workspaces values as the inherited base. The title also follows a conventional commit format and includes the tracking ID. It omits the screenshot policy binding and the new Settings UI, but it does not need to cover every detail.
Full details: Description check
**Explanation** The description covers the purpose, the resolver design, the capture-policy behavior, the UI, the design decisions, the deviations from the mock, and the verification steps. It links the ADR and the Linear issue. The required "What to review" section is missing. The template asks for three to five anchored entries in the form file.ts:line, and the description has none. It also has no manual verification checklist. The Checks section has test counts but no output for `bun run check-types` and `bun run test` in the template form. The "Decisions worth a look" section partly covers review focus, but it is not the required section and gives no file:line anchors. **Resolution** Add a "What to review" section with three to five entries. Anchor each entry to a file and line, such as `apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/workspace-settings.ts:NN`. State what the reviewer should decide. Name the files that are safe to skim, such as the i18n JSON pairs and the generated test fixtures. Add the template's "Checks" lines with the actual `bun run check-types` and `bun run test` output. Add a "Manual verification" section with unchecked boxes for the items the suite cannot cover, such as the UI layout in Electron and the sheet appearance. Keep the CLA note if this PR is from someone other than the maintainer.

Documentation-only edits and deletions within surviving functions are included; unchanged diff context and fully deleted functions are excluded. Review items from CodeRabbit's last pass that sit outside a diff thread (all at d9accc88):

- **Do not overwrite an unreadable machine settings file** (real, major). `MachineSettingsStore` now treats only a missing file as empty. Any other read failure is remembered: `update` tries the read once more and, if the file still cannot be read, rejects without writing, so the other workspaces' records survive. Tests: an unreadable path is never written over; the next update heals once the file reads again.
- **Refuse the copy when the source file is unreadable** (real, major). `copyToAll` now answers `{ ok: false, reason: "unreadable" }` before the All level or any other workspace is touched. Test: a source with a broken `settings.json` writes nothing anywhere.
- **Wait for the old read to finish before the write starts** (trivial, real). The race test now signals when the stale bytes are in hand before it starts the write.
- **Notify PendingSettingsHost when a pending folder file is discovered** (minor, declined). A capture that finds a changed file does not change the effective settings, so it sends no broadcast and the sheet waits for the next trigger. That is what the spec asks for ("the next time the workspace is active", and a capture never waits on the answer), and the capture hides the window, so the host re-reads on the window's focus when the user comes back. A dedicated notification would add a channel for a gap of seconds.
